learning_outcomes.text: Be able to analyze and solve machine maintenance problems.
Be able to solve maintenance problems as a team member, both as a coordinator and as a coordinated member.
Be able to infer other maintenance problems based on previously solved problems.
Be able to evaluate the overall operational status of a machine.
Be able to apply theoretical knowledge to the practice of mechanical maintenance.
Be able to solve common mechanical element maintenance problems.
Be able to carry out specific machine maintenance tasks.
Be able to design, execute, and evolve the integral preventive/predictive maintenance plan for an industrial plant.

syllabus_topics: Practical seminar: Analysis of lubricants and maintenance of belt transmissions
Practical seminar: Diagnosis by vibration measurement and rotor balancing
Practical session: Inspection and tuning of a belt transmission
Practical session: Bearing assembly and disassembly techniques
Practical session: Shaft adaptation and alignment
Practical session: Balancing a rotor by vibration measurement

assessment_methods.method: Final exam on the theoretical part

assessment_rules: To pass the course, students must obtain an overall average of at least 5 out of 10. In the first attempt, the final theory exam has a minimum score of 4 out of 10; failure to meet this minimum results in an overall average not exceeding 4.5. For the second attempt, continuous assessment comprises 30% (lab practicals 10%, practical work 20%), while a questionnaire on practicals (20%) and the final theory exam (50%, with a minimum of 4/10) are conducted on the exam day. Practical work is recoverable for the second attempt if the first attempt score is below 4/10, and the questionnaire on practicals is obligatorily included in the final exam of the second attempt.
